prompt: The polynomial $p$ is defined by $p(x) = x^3 - 4x$. Which of the following is a factor of $p(x)$?
hint: Look at the two terms of $p(x)$. They share a common factor, and removing it is the natural first step.

hints.text: Look at the two terms of $p(x)$. They share a common factor, and removing it is the natural first step.
Taking out $x$ gives $x(x^2 - 4)$. The bracket $x^2 - 4$ is a difference of squares, so factor it once more.
The full factorization is $p(x) = x(x + 2)(x - 2)$, so $x - 2$ is a factor, which is choice B.

learningObjective: Factor a cubic by extracting a common term and a difference of squares.
explanation: Both terms contain $x$, so factor it out first: $x^3 - 4x = x(x^2 - 4)$.
The bracket is a difference of squares because $4 = 2^2$, so $x^2 - 4 = (x + 2)(x - 2)$.
The complete factorization is $p(x) = x(x + 2)(x - 2)$, and none of the other choices appears in it.
The factor among the choices is $x - 2$, which is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test each candidate with the Factor Theorem
steps: $(x - a)$ is a factor exactly when $p(a) = 0$.
Test $a = 4$: $p(4) = 64 - 16 = 48 \neq 0$ ✗. Substituting is often faster than factoring when the choices are handed to you.
